To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a COTS ITMS based E TD can be interfaced to a MS/MS instrument for the characterization of the gas phase chemistry of the instrument and that the ion trapping scheme in this instrument increases predominant ion intensities.

the predominant ion chemistry of a COTS ITMS based E TD is determined by proton abstraction, ion molecule attachment, autoionizati on, first-order and second-order thermolysis and nucleophilic substi tution.

the gas phase ion reactions in the reaction region (ion trap) of the ITMS based explosive trace detector are complex and include proton abstraction, attachment, autoionizaiton, thermolysis, nucleophilic substitution, and ion-molecule reactions.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development and application of tandem mass spectrometric techniques for the fundamental characterization of the gas phase chemistry intrinsic to the operation of a COTS ITMS based E TD.

the gas phase ion-molecule chemistry intrinsic to the COTS ITMS instrument and the results are expected to be applicable to other ITMS instruments as well as to other types of ion mobility spectrometers.
the fundamental understanding of the ionization processes in an ITMS based ECD and is intended to provide the basis for the development and optimization of the next generation ITMS based ETCs.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the ionization processes in this particular ITMS based ETC are dominated by proton transfer reactions and that the ion trapping scheme in this particular ITMSETC increases product ion intensities relative non-ion trap operation, which is consistent with the results reported in the literature for the ion trap mobility spectrometer.
the ion chemistry of the ITMS based explosive trace detector is complex and involves the formation of numerous product and daughter ions.
the gas phase ion-molecule chemistry intrinsic to the COTS ITMS based E TD is complex and involves a variety of ionization processes.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the ITMS instrument operates via a complex ionization scheme that involves a variety of ion-molecule reactions, autoionization reactions, and ion-molecule attachment reactions.
we have demonstrated that the ion trap mobility spectrometer can be used to ionize a wide variety of explosive compounds.
the ITMS instrument can be considered a gas phase ion trap mass spectrometer (ITMS-MS) that is capable of producing a wide variety of product ions from a single ionization source.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the ion chemistry in the ITMS ETD is complex and involves a multitude of ionization and reaction processes.

the ITMS based explosives detector is an extremely sensitive and selective detector capable of detecting and distinguishing between various nitro, nitrite, and peroxide based explosives at the low parts per billion (ppb) level.
the ITMS instrument can be considered a multi-ionization source, with the predominant ionization mechanism being dependent on the analyte.
